extracted.intended_audience: editors/collectors of traditional ballads; literary scholars and students of folklore
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for collecting, collating, annotating, and publishing traditional ballads from multiple manuscript and oral variants, with attention to authenticity, modernization, and explanatory notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collation and selection of a collated edition
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor found it easy to collect a variety of copies; but very difficult, indeed, to select from them such a collated edition, as may, in any degree, suit the taste of 'these more light and giddy-paced times.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect multiple copies (oral and manuscript), collate variants, and make a careful selection to form a coherent edition. Balance fidelity to sources with readability for contemporary audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernization of language (with caution)
rubrics_metrics.description: The language has been gradually modernized, in the course of its transmission to us, through the inaccurate channel of oral tradition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that variants may reflect gradual modernization by oral transmission; modernize language where necessary for comprehension but indicate changes and preserve vestiges of original forms when important for meaning or authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for oral-transmission distortions
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmission ... through the inaccurate channel of oral tradition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat orally transmitted variants as products of transmission noise; do not assume a single 'original' text without corroborating evidence. Report variant readings and note probable corruptions or alterations arising from oral performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve poetic economy — avoid unnecessary minute detail
rubrics_metrics.description: The bard does not relate particulars, but barely the striking outlines of a fact, apparently so well known when he wrote, as to render minute detail as unnecessary, as it is always tedious and unpoetical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When editing or presenting ballads, preserve their characteristic concision and focus on striking outlines; avoid inserting excessive explanatory detail into the text itself (use notes instead).

rubrics_metrics.name: Select stanzas 'of most merit' from multiple sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The stanzas appearing to possess most merit have been selected from each copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple versions exist, choose stanzas that best serve poetic quality, narrative coherence, and authenticity; document provenance of selected lines and note omissions or replacements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use conjectural emendation sparingly and transparently
rubrics_metrics.description: This Ballad is published ... partly from a MS. of some antiquity ... This ballad is published from tradition, with some conjectural emendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply conjectural emendations only where necessary (e.g., clear corruption or lacuna), base changes on comparison with other copies, and indicate emendations in apparatus or notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve established proper names; avoid gratuitous alterations
rubrics_metrics.description: There can be no reason, even were internal evidence totally wanting, for altering a well known proper name, which, till of late years, has been the uniform title of the ballad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not alter traditional proper names (e.g., Gil Morrice) to modern or mistaken forms without compelling justification; preserve names that form part of the ballad's identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotate dialect, archaic terms, and obscure references
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes explain terms such as 'Redding kain--Comb for the hair', 'Cosh--Quiet', 'Brash--Sickness', etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explanatory footnotes or glosses for dialect words, archaic usages, and culturally specific items so readers can understand, while keeping the original wording in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize via comparative and classical parallels
rubrics_metrics.description: Those, who wish to know how an incantation, or charm, of the distressing nature here described, may consult the story of Galanthis's Metamorphosis, in Ovid ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place ballad motifs and devices in a broader literary and mythological context by citing analogous classical, continental, or folkloric sources to illuminate meaning and provenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use local/traditional and material evidence to identify events/subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor was therefore led to suppose, that the hero of the ballad might have been identified with John Scott ... This appeared the more probable, as the common people always affirm ... In ploughing Annan's Treat, a huge monumental stone, with an inscription, was discovered ... it probably records the event of the combat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corroborate oral tradition with local history, heraldry, inscriptions, or monuments when attempting to identify persons, places, or historical events associated with a ballad; report the strength and limits of such evidence.
